newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 6.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Monday:
Talks continued to end the prison hostage siege in which six inmates of Dublin's Mountjoy jail took four warders hostage.
Loyalists plan a terror campaign in the Irish Republic involving a wage of revenge firebomb attacks to retaliate for IRA violence., according to a source in the outlawed Ulster Freedom Fighters.
Prison authorities took a "softly softly" approach to try to end the hostage siege at Dublin's Mountjoy prison.
Coach Murray Kidd seems certain to lose his job as Ireland's Rugby coach after his side's 37-29 humiliation by lowly Italy at the weekend.
A joyrider was killed and two people were injured when a stolen car went out of control on a narrow Dublin road.
Irish Rugby coach Murray Kidd is to be replaced after Italy beat Ireland on Saturday.
The department of justice has agreed to investigate complaints by six prisoners holding hostages at Dublin's Mountjoy jail.
Former Prime Minister Albert Reynolds is to be offered a key non-ministerial post in the Northern Ireland peace process if his Fianna Fail party wins general elections due by November this year.
